MATERIAL LIBRARY / 06 SPECIMENS

A different way to break.

Material responses share the same solver. Aging changes what survives it.

All coefficients are editable game-design approximations; relay crystal is fictional. The lab uses effective scalar capacity, not finite-element analysis.

MODEL NOTES / SCOPE & ASSUMPTIONS

A world-system workbench.

A compact, inspectable implementation of Rose’s physics requirements.

01

Forces & motion

Each lab proxy is a mass on a damped spring, integrated at 60 Hz. This is a separate browser study; the archived Python engine uses a broader planar solver and its own 1/256 model-time step. Impact transfers a 0.12-second impulse; wind, sustained load, and seismic forcing act over time. Angle resolves lateral force; friction opposes motion. Tilt follows displacement and lever height.

m·a = F − k·x − c·v − Fμ

Ground collisions, gravity, restitution, and sliding friction animate debris. The water pump, power rotor, and canopy respond to time, wind, and structural integrity. These are 2.5D procedural proxies, ready for future prefab art. Pause freezes motion; reduced motion uses stable poses and debris while preserving the same computed results.

02

Aging & failure

Age, weather exposure, use, and material susceptibility reduce baseline integrity. Aged capacity scales with the square of baseline integrity. Force above a tuned stress threshold accumulates damage; critical damage or excessive tilt creates rubble.

capacity = strength × effective section × aged integrity² × fatigue

Age is an equivalent weathering parameter, not a real-life service forecast. Repair spends 2% of specimen mass in maintenance input to remove up to 25% load damage, retaining age. Collapse disconnects service and blocks a footprint. Once-only salvage credits the material stock; rebuilding spends a full specimen mass. Setup changes and Reset explicitly start a fresh sandbox allocation.

03

Scale & terrain

Lab proxy cores are 8.4–10.8 m tall: 4.7–6.0 times the 1.8 m reference person. The camera keeps the source’s orthographic 0.52 ground compression. Human-scale service hatches anchor their apparent size. Causeways and canopies use their own functional proportions.

The terrain is rendered as continuous irregular landforms and paths. Hex coordinates form a separate tactical overlay. Toggle the lattice without changing terrain or structures; Detail, Site, and Landscape use the same world geometry.

04

What this prototype covers

Material selection, aging, collisions, friction, spring/damper response, force-derived torque, collapse animation, service loss, finite salvage, repair/rebuild, terrain inspection, before/after comparison, and visual review.

General rigid-body assemblies, fluid dynamics, full terrain navigation, saved-world networking, prefab character animation, and VREX–TETHER are outside this lab build. No energy-extraction claims or hidden scientific measurements are simulated.

Configuration, the current specimen, and visual-review choices persist in this browser. No external analytics, remote assets, or physics service is used. Export produces a JSON snapshot with the current setup and results.
